ideas.name: 瓷脊灵狐
ideas.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. MagicDesk original living mechanical sculpture concept, explicitly inspired by Atomic Heart's elegant Soviet retrofuturist laboratory biotechnology, not a replica of any game character. Milk-white glazed porcelain shell, exposed precise nickel skeleton, dark steel, small red enamel joints and warm amber/red optical accents. Give it a sense of life through its pose and anatomy, not cartoon eyes, fur, a smiley face or a glowing orb.

Reference image is the existing HELIOS pedestal and palette. Replace ONLY the UPPER egg with the new sculpture, KEEP the EXACT shared low circular stepped pedestal outer shell, diameter and height, unchanged. Base diameter D=2.74 scene units and fixed base height=.670608 (0.245D). Never make the base wider, taller, narrower or add tiers to fit the creature. One single common circular mounting deck and one separate red X exit control at the far right. The central curved operation cassette may have controls specific to this creature, but inside the same front fascia height. No standalone model-selection button: the selector trigger is a flush section of the existing metal rim. These are design concepts, not dimensionally verified manufacturing drawings.

Wide 3:2 premium charcoal studio concept board. Three consistent views, with EXACT SAME base scale and camera magnification across states: a large left hero 'REST', top right 'GREETING', bottom right 'ASSEMBLY'. Small title exactly as specified. Show complete creature and pedestal, no cropped base, no floating base. For the right-hand small views use extra negative space as needed; don't resize the pedestal relative to the creature. All body parts attached, credible mechanical pivots. The creature remains on the pedestal in every normal state. No drone, weapons, blue-purple hologram UI, fur, cute toy proportions or generic pet robot.
UPPER CREATURE: PORCELAIN VULPINE, an elegant slender biomechanical FOX with exactly FOUR articulated legs, two pointed independently hinged porcelain ears, long narrow muzzle with a small dark nickel scent intake, tiny recessed amber iris lenses, and one long expressive tail made of overlapping ivory ceramic vertebral segments. A flexible visible nickel spine, subtle bellows at throat, split porcelain shoulder and hip plates. Proportions dignified and uncanny, not a chibi, plush toy, cartoon or realistic living fox. Upper creature total height from mounting deck at most .9D; curled tail and all four paws stay within the base footprint in rest. Tiny integrated foot magnetic pads attach paws to the unchanged mounting deck, no large extra stand.

REST: fox curled in a compact seated resting pose, head turned as if listening, one ear angled differently, tail curves around feet. One front paw lightly raised above the deck but other paws support it.
GREETING: same fox rises slightly on all four legs, ears turn first, head tilts toward viewer, forequarters stretch forward with toes on the deck and tail articulates into a graceful question-mark curve within about 1.35D total envelope. Same four legs, same tail segments, no extra limbs.
ASSEMBLY: tail spine, head with ears, forelimb pair, rear limb pair, torso porcelain panels and central spine separated along logical joint axes; keep the common base intact. Use a clear limited number of real modules, not many random screws.

Creature-specific control cassette: two ear-shaped ivory rocker paddles (listen / greet), a short ribbed gesture wheel and a small curved rest latch. Fixed red X at far right. Personality is alert, reserved and gradually trusting. Title exactly 'E2  PORCELAIN VULPINE'.

All body parts attached, credible mechanical pivots. The creature remains on the pedestal in every normal state. UPPER CREATURE: CABINET HERMIT, a curious NON-ANIMAL-specific mechanical lifeform reminiscent of a hermit that lives in a porcelain laboratory sample capsule. A compact smooth asymmetric IVORY SEED-CABINET shell sits low over a little body on exactly FOUR short jointed nickel support limbs. One small expressive periscope-like head on a flexible segmented neck peeks from a clearly bounded front shutter; the head has a single dark lens with an adjustable mechanical iris, not a human eye. Two little unequal feeler probes beside the head. The shell is NOT a spiral seashell: it is a rounded oblong rigid instrument housing with THREE ceramic sliding shutters and visible red locking catches, tiny ribs and vents. Body plus shell fits within .85D wide and .8D high above the shared deck. All four support feet stay on the same pedestal. It must look like an unfamiliar living laboratory apparatus, shy and inquisitive, not a surveillance camera, tank, toy crab, insect drone or humanoid.

REST: cabinet shutter almost closed, head half withdrawn and tilted, one feeler quietly out. Shell huddled over its four folded legs, giving a guarded creature posture.
GREETING: same four legs extend a little to lift the shell, head comes out and tilts sideways; two small front manipulator fingers (attached to the head support, distinct from the four support legs) gently test the edge of the shell; three shutters part slightly to reveal moving nickel bellows and a small optical calibrator, not a sun core. Warm red light tracks through slots like breathing. Curious shy greeting rather than aggressive attack.
ASSEMBLY: three outer ceramic shutter modules, head/neck cartridge, four leg modules and inner bellows assembly separate on their mount axes, maintaining a coherent cabinet skeleton; pedestal unchanged.

Creature-specific control cassette: an aperture lever in a curved slot, a ridged ivory curiosity wheel with three detents, and two small rectangular invitation/rest keys. Same separate red X. Personality expressed by hesitant timing, head retreat, feeler responses and progressive emergence. Title exactly 'E3  CABINET HERMIT'.
